title: Sahara Silence
subtitle: Vast heat, shifting dunes, and the pulse of ancient wind

chapters.label: CHAPTER 01 · BOUNDARIES
chapters.heading: A continent of sand stretches to the horizon
chapters.body: The Sahara spans North Africa, covering 9,200,000 square kilometres (3,600,000 sq mi). It is the largest hot desert and the third‑largest desert overall, smaller only than Antarctica and the northern Arctic. The dunes stretch from the Red Sea in the east, the Mediterranean in the north, to the Atlantic in the west, while the Sahel marks its southern edge.

chapters.label: CHAPTER 02 · MOUNTAINS
chapters.heading: Rock and fire rise from endless dunes
chapters.body: The Sahara’s terrain mixes hamada rocky plateaus, ergs of sweeping sand seas, reg gravel plains and dry valleys that carve the surface. Dunes climb over 180 metres (590 ft). Volcanic massifs punctuate the horizon, the Aïr, Ahaggar and Tibesti ranges, with Emi Koussi, a shield volcano, standing as the desert’s highest summit.

heroImage.attribution: Sergey Pesterev · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

chapters.label: CHAPTER 03 · CLIMATE
chapters.heading: Sun dominates a sky without clouds
chapters.body: Situated in the horse latitudes, the Sahara sits beneath a subtropical ridge that forces air to descend, warm and dry, erasing clouds. The result is relentless sunshine and virtually no rain, especially across the eastern Libyan Desert, one of the planet’s driest zones. Continental tropical air masses dominate, while a seasonal thermal low deepens the heat in summer.
